title: Haplotype analysis of the CDS in Arabidopsis thaliana
author: Magdalena M Julkowska
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.i2gcgbw

steps.title: Download gene sequences
steps.instruction: Download the coding sequences (CDS) of the gene of interest for all HapMap accessions from the 1001 Genomes SALK Genome Browser (http://signal.salk.edu/atg1001/index.php) and save the file in a text editor, removing all "[", "]", and "-" characters while keeping dots that represent missing data. Additional genotypes can be obtained from http://tools.1001genomes.org/2.

steps.title: Highlight CDS in uppercase
steps.instruction: Ensure that the gene of interest is highlighted and that the entire CDS is written in capital letters; this is essential for downstream processing.

steps.title: Save as plain‑text file
steps.instruction: Save the edited sequence file as a plain‑text document with a ".txt" extension.

steps.title: Open terminal and navigate
steps.instruction: Open a terminal window and change to the directory containing the .txt files.

substeps.instruction: Enter: cd /Users/julkowmm/Desktop/Haplotype (replace with your own path if different).

steps.title: Extract CDS only
steps.instruction: Run the following command to remove all lower‑case letters (non‑CDS nucleotides) and dots, producing a file that contains only the CDS sequences:

substeps.instruction: cat AT5G66270_Zink_finger_CDS.txt | perl -e '$count=1; foreach $line () {if ($count==1) {print $line; $count=$count+1;} elsif ($line=~/>/) {print "\n$line";} else {chomp $line; print $line; }}' | sed -e 's/^.*rev//g' | sed '/^>/! s/[atgc]//g' | sed -e 's/\.//g' > AT5G66270_Zink_finger_protein.txt
Replace "AT5G66270_Zink_finger_CDS.txt" and "AT5G66270_Zink_finger_protein.txt" with the actual names of your input and output files.

steps.title: Collapse sequences with FaBox
steps.instruction: Upload the CDS‑only file to the FaBox DNA‑to‑haplotype collapser and converter (http://users-birc.au.dk/biopv/php/fabox/), click the appropriate tool, paste the sequences, and run the collapse to obtain individual haplotype sequences.

steps.title: Download haplotype and phenotype files
steps.instruction: Download the resulting individual haplotype sequences and the accompanying file that maps each accession to its phenotype.

steps.title: Translate haplotypes to protein
steps.instruction: Install JalView (http://www.jalview.org/), load the DNA haplotype sequences, and use JalView’s translation function to obtain the corresponding protein sequences.

steps.title: Remove identical protein haplotypes
steps.instruction: Sort the aligned protein sequences by pairwise comparison and eliminate any haplotypes that are exactly identical at the protein level.

steps.title: Remove redundant haplotypes
steps.instruction: From the original input file, delete redundant haplotypes that were collapsed in the previous step. Keep a record of which haplotypes were merged to avoid confusion later.

steps.title: Assign accessions to haplotype groups
steps.instruction: Match each accession to its specific haplotype group as identified by the FaBox collapser, updating the list if further collapsing based on amino‑acid identity is possible.

steps.title: Link haplotypes to phenotypes
steps.instruction: Combine the accession‑to‑haplotype mapping with the phenotype data to create a table that shows which haplotype group each phenotype belongs to.

steps.title: Identify significant haplotype groups
steps.instruction: Examine the phenotype differences between haplotype groups, considering only groups that contain three or more genotypes (smaller groups are unreliable).

steps.title: Isolate interesting haplotype sequences
steps.instruction: Select the haplotypes that show the most significant phenotype differences and export their amino‑acid sequences to a separate ".txt" file.

steps.title: Color amino acids in JalView
steps.instruction: Import the ".txt" file of the selected haplotypes into JalView and colour the amino acids using the ClustalX colour scheme.

steps.title: Format final alignment
steps.instruction: Wrap the alignment text, add scale bars above, below and to the right, include boxes and gap symbols, ensure the alignment is exactly 125 amino acids long, and export the figure as a PDF.

steps.title: Annotate protein domains
steps.instruction: Search UniProt (http://www.uniprot.org/) for known domains of the protein, mark these domains on the PDF alignment, and note any sequence alterations in the different haplotypes.

steps.title: Select haplotypes for cloning
steps.instruction: Choose the most interesting haplotypes for cloning and allele‑complementation experiments, based on the observed phenotype differences and protein‑sequence variation.
